cards.title: Parenting Is Hard. Should We Let AI Do It?
cards.body: Tech companies offer eye-movement trackers, personalized podcasts and 'optimized nap predictions' to help parents. But do families actually need these gadgets, or are they solving problems that don't exist?

cards.title: Second Baby Brain: What You Forget
cards.body: A parent discovers that having a second child means relearning everything about feeding, teething, and sleep routines. The childhood they remember as 'blissfully bored' looks very different the second time around.

cards.title: The '18 Summers' Parenting Trend Debate
cards.body: Summer holidays with nothing to do is the whole point of childhood, but the trend of turning summers into 'memory-making exercises' feels creepy and controlling. Long, unstructured days matter more than optimized activities.

cards.title: Your Quiet Child May Be Overwhelmed
cards.body: The child who screams gets everyone's attention, but the silent child may need just as much help. Adults often miss distress that looks like 'nothing' instead of obvious meltdowns.

cards.title: Five Reasons Your Emotions Matter as a Parent
cards.body: Your emotional life directly affects your connection with your children. Understanding your own feelings helps you model healthy emotional development.

cards.title: Motherhood and Women's Mental Health
cards.body: The Lindsay Clancy trial reveals deeper questions about how society judges motherhood, women's mental health, and what defines a 'good mother'. Legal outcomes reflect cultural expectations about maternal behavior.
